chapter: New Orleans trombone style and composing
title: Ory's Creole Trombone at Mardi Gras
summary: With Paul he plays Ory's Creole Trombone on the street; he bought the music, never saw Ory, and Russell recalls interviewing him in California.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well I don't have too many of them. About two or three of them. And I got the other two I have in mind I don't have no title for them. Mm-hmm. Now Paul and I got to get on the slide for a slide because when I got with them at the Mardi Gras a lot of people used to ask for
Ur's trombone. Oh yeah. Ur's Creole trombone.

Well you know out there on the street I mean take a tune like Ur's Creole trombone. Well I mean you got to feel them things you know. Yeah just start to know trick things that he does. Yeah well I mean he can do more justice with it than uh than anyone else. Well you didn't have no time to rehearsal. And you know the man don't want no music sitting up there. Yeah. So we got together and said well we're going to get the tune. So we Paul had a pretty good idea on regs. Mm-hmm. So we got together and well I feel that. Yeah it's a good number. Yeah. Yeah I feel that. I didn't really feel that. But now I, now matter of fact I bought the music to uh uh Ur's trombone. Oh I didn't know it was published that. Yeah I got it. I got a stock on it.
I didn't even know. I knew he had the uh Musgrave Rambles Savoy Blues published. I didn't know that.
And it come out. Yeah. Yeah he got that. He got the stock on it.
It's nice. Did you ever get to hear Ur's in person?
Never did. Never did see him. Really?

Uh-uh. He was down here about four almost more like six years ago. I think he went through here when his sister died and was here a couple of days is all. But hardly anybody saw him that I've taught. Never did see him Bill. We interviewed him uh two years ago in California. Yeah. Professor Minetta was out there with him.
That's a good. I love him man. He's nice. Professor Minetta. He's taught a lot of musicians around here. Yeah I like him. Nice fella.

Now I never get a chance to hear the issues. Yeah, or he was around Chicago a lot. I heard him in late days only from 1940. I met him when I was in California in 1940. He was playing bass then. Started giving up trombone and he came back a couple years later on trombone.
